full_judgment:
(1) The Court of Appeal committed an error of law in holding that the onus of proof was upon the plaintiff that the alleged deed of gift was collusively obtained from her. 

 (2) Since the plaintiff was a pardanashin lady a special rule of onus is applicable and it is settled principle of law that a person claiming benefit under a document executed by a pardanashin lady, the burden of proof is upon the donee to show that the donor had independent advice and she properly understood the terms of the deed before its execution. 

 (1) It is settled principle of law that burden of proof lies upon the plaintiff to prove his case and that who alleges forgery he must prove it but in the instant case the plaintiff has failed to prove her case. 

 (7) There is a presumption of a registered document under the Registration Act and since the deed in question is a registered deed it is presumed to be correctly executed and registered and since the plaintiff alleges that the gift was obtained by misrepresentation the burden was upon the plaintiff to prove her case but she failed to do so and accordingly, the Court of appeal rightly held that the deed of gift was a genuine document. 

 11. Admittedly, the predecessor of the present petitioners and opposite parties, namely Most. Nurnahar Bewa had no issue and she had some properties of her own. She brought the suit for cancellation of registered deed of gift No. 10426 dated 16-10-1978 in respect of the suit property, which was claimed to be transferred to her brother, the defendant Ataur Rahman, on the allegation that by taking advantage of her position her brother obtained the deed of gift by misrepresentation. It has specifically contended in the plaint that terms of the deed of gift were not read over and explained to her at the time of its execution and registration. Both the Courts below dismissed the suit taking the view that Most. Nurnahar Bewa was not a pardanashin lady and she executed and registered the deed of gift in favour of the defendant at her free will and the burden of proof was upon her that the impugned transaction was collusive and void. 

 12. The main considerations before this Court are, whether the plaintiff was a pardanashin lady and whether the burden of proof was upon her that the impugned transaction was collusive and void. 

 "111.—Proof of good faith in transactions where one party is in relation of active confidence—Where there is a question as to the good faith of transaction between parties, one of whom stands to the other in a position of active confidence, the burden of proving the good faith of the transaction is on the party who is in a position of active confidence." 

 16. It is the mandate of section 111 of the Evidence Act that the burden of proving of good faith shall be cast upon the person who relies on the transaction if a relationship of 'active confidence' or 'fiduciary relationship' subsists between the parties. The word 'active confidence' in this section indicates that the relationship between the parties must be such that one is bound to protect the interest of the other. 

 If in a case of a transfer by a pardanashin lady a dispute arises as to its validity, the onus is always on the party who seeks to hold the transferor to the terms of the deed to satisfy the Court on evidence that she substantially understood the disposition and she executed the deed with full understanding of what she was doing and of the nature and effect of the transaction. It is to be observed that independent advice by itself is not an essential burden to be discharged, unless there are some Special circumstances calling for its application, in that the donee or the transferee stood in a position of active confidence or had fiduciary relationship with the pardanashin lady. It is only in such cases, the donee or transferee will carry the additional burden or to prove that the lady had independent and disinterested advice from persons other than the recipient of the document. 

 19. To make the disposition by a pardanashin lady a valid one it must be proved that the disposition was substantially understood and it was really the mental act of the person who made it. The rule of law as indicated above is an exception of general rules. The rule of law has been codified in section 111 of the Evidence Act, which provides that where there is a question as to the good faith of a transaction between the parties, one of whom stands to the other in a position of active confidence, the burden of proving the good faith of the transaction is on the party who is in a position of active confidence. Relationship between the pardanashin woman and the person in fiduciary relationship, who is the donee, raises the presumption of influence upon the pardanashin lady and the burden is upon the donee to show that the act was spontaneous. 

 24. Whether the plaintiff was a pardanashin lady or not is a question of fact but the Court of appeal, upon misreading and non-consideration of evidence and misconception of law, came to erroneous finding that the plaintiff was not a pardanashin lady. The Court of Appeal should have came to the conclusion that the plaintiff was a pardanashin lady and the burden was upon the defendant to prove that the disputed deed of gift was explained to her, she understood the contents of the deed by disinterested person which is lacking in this case.
